key_insight: An LLM-driven evolutionary search can discover interpretable fermion-to-qubit encodings with verified code distance beyond prior GSE limits, reaching exact distance 5 and even 6 on one molecular instance.
engineering_relevance: The resulting encodings reduce qubit overhead and improve logical-failure rates for molecular simulation benchmarks, making them attractive as resource-efficient wrappers around quantum chemistry workloads.
method: LLM edits a constructor program for the GSE encoding
An external verifier scores exact stabilizer-coset distance and retains high performers
A second search uses verifier feedback to optimize compression while preserving verified distance
evidence_signal: On tested molecular instances, the search produced exact distance-5 codes and one distance-6 code, and at p=10^-3 the encodings used 4.2–5.0× fewer data qubits with 3.4–8.2× lower logical-failure rates versus the comparison route.
watch_item: Results are limited to verified encoding-level metrics; the paper does not claim circuit-level fault tolerance, Trotter-cost improvements, or guaranteed scaling beyond the tested instances.
paper_title: Evolving Quantum Error-Correcting Encodings for Molecular Simulation
